title: Zero-consistency root emulation for unprivileged container image build
problem: Container image builds require privileged operations, preventing unprivileged container workflows. Linux package managers request root-level system calls during Dockerfile builds, creating barriers to fully unprivileged container construction.
motivation: Unprivileged container building is essential for secure and practical HPC application deployment in shared cluster environments.
method: A Linux seccomp filter intercepts privileged system calls during container image builds and returns success without executing them. The filter transparently fakes successful execution, allowing package managers to proceed without root access or consistency requirements, enabling builds of Dockerfiles that standard Docker cannot construct.
key_novelty: Using seccomp filtering to fake successful privileged operations enables unprivileged container builds without maintaining any consistency in the emulated system calls.
contributions: A seccomp-based root emulation technique for unprivileged container image construction
Demonstrates compatibility with diverse Dockerfiles, including containers that Docker itself cannot build
Eliminates privilege barriers for HPC application containerization workflows
limitations: No consistency guarantees in emulated operations; broader performance and compatibility implications not discussed.
primary_theme: Seccomp-based privilege emulation for unprivileged container builds
